v: pu॰ kanyAH kubjAH yatra । kAnyakubjadeSe hema॰ “kanyAkubje'pibat somamindreRa saha kOSikaH” BA॰ va॰ 27 a॰ । kanyAnAM saMGaH aR kAnyaM tat kubjaM yatra kA nyakubjo'pyatra । yaTA ca taddeSe kanyAnAM vAyunA kubjatvaM kftaM yaTA varRitam rAmA॰ A॰ kARqe । “kuSanABastu rAjarziH kanyASatamanuttamam । janayAmAsa DarmmAtmA GftAcyAM raGunandana! । tAstu yOvanaSAlinyo rUpavatyaH svalaNkftAH । udyAnaBUmimAgamya prAdfzIva SatahradAH । gAyantyo nftyamAnASca vAdayantyastu rAGava! । AmodaM paramaM jagmurvarABaraRaBUzitAH । aTa tAScArusarvvANgyo rUpeRApratiBA Buvi । udyAnaBUmimAgamya tArA iva GanAntare । tAH sarvvA guRasampagrA rUpayOvanasaMyutAH । dfzwvA sarvvAtmako vAyuridaM vacanamabravIt । ahaM vaH kAmaye sarvvA BAryyA mama BavizyaTa । mAnupastyajyatAM BAvo dIrGamAyuravApsyaTaH calaM hi yOvanaM nityaM mAnuzezu viSezataH । akzayaM yOvanaM prAptA amaryyaSca BavizyaTa । tasya tadvacanaM SrutvA vAyoraklizwakarmmaRaH । apahasya tato vAkyaM kanyASatamaTAbravIt । antaScarasi BUtAnAM sarvvezAM murasattama! । praBAvajYASca te sarvvAH kimarTamavamanyase । kuSanABasutAdeva! samastAH surasattama! । sTAnAccyAvayituM devaM rakzAmastu tapo vayam । mA mUt sa kAlo durmmeDaH! pitaraM satyavAdinam । avamanya svaDarBoRa KayaM varamupAsmahe । pitA hi praBurasmAkaM dEvataM paramaYca saH । yasya no dAsyati pitA sa no BarttA Bavizyati । tAsAM tu vacanaM SrutvA hariH paramakopanaH । praviSya sarvagAtrARi baBaYja BagavAn praBuH । tAH kanyA vAyunA BambA viviSurnfpatergfham । praviSya ca susamBrAntAH salajjAH sASrulocanAH । sa ca tA dayitA BagnAH kanyAH paramaSoBanAH । dfzwvA dIvastadA rAjA samBrAnta imadabravIt । kimidaM kaTyatAM puttryaH! ko Darmamavamanyate । kubjAH kena kftAH sarvvAScezwantyo nABiBAzata” ।

(f(आ). , L.), N. of an ancient city of great note (in the north-western provinces of India, situated on the काली नदी, a branch of the Gaṅgā, in the modern district of Farrukhabad; the popular spelling of the name presents, perhaps, greater variations than that of any place in India [e.g. Kanauj, Kunnoj, Kunnouj, Kinoge, Kinnoge, Kinnauj, Kanoj, Kannauj, Kunowj, Canowj Canoje, Canauj, &c.]; in antiquity this city ranks next to Ayodhyā in Oude; it is known in classical geography as Canogyza; but the name applies also to its dependencies and the surrounding district; the current etymology [कन्या, ‘a girl’, shortened to कन्य, and कुब्ज, ‘round-shouldered or crooked’] refers to a legend in R. i, 32, 11 ff., relating to the hundred daughters of Kuśanābha, the king of this city, who were all rendered crooked by Vāyu for non-compliance with his licentious desires; the ruins of the ancient city are said to occupy a site larger than that of London), MBh.; Kathās. &c.
